alex_support: Hey team — customer @carol is seeing embedding dims flip when they send mixed payloads (single string + array) to /v1/embeddings. They expect 768 but some items come back 512. Reported in production at 2025-11-03T18:04Z. Request IDs: req_8a3f1c2b, req_8a3f1c2c, req_8a3f1d00. Can we collect repro steps and a debug bundle?

sara_ml: Thanks Alex. Do we have the exact request bodies and headers? Suspect batching path might be picking a smaller model variant or truncating vector dim on KV-cache boundary.

carol_customer: pasted the two failing requests below. One was a multipart batch (1 short + 4 long), other was 5x singles in parallel. We see 3/5 vectors at 768, 2/5 at 512 on the batch.

carol_customer: ```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-v1",
  "input": ["short", "very long text ... repeated ..." , "another long ...", "long 3", "long 4"],
  "batch_hint": 5
}
```

alex_support: Helpful — thanks. Jordan, can infra pull logs for those req IDs and enable debug trace for serving-runtime for ~10m. Also ask customer to reproduce with a curl we can share so we have exact headers.

jordan_infra: On it. I see req_8a3f1c2b hitting node gpu-12 and req_8a3f1c2c routed to gpu-3. Logs show: `WARN runtime.batch: stride_mismatch detected for batch_id=0x7f2a, choosing fallback kernel; output_dim=512` around the same window. Pushing a debug config now (trace=rpc,serve,quant).

alex_support: Carol — can you run this curl (it forces single explicit batching that mirrors your client) and paste the response IDs?

alex_support: ```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-v1","input":["short","very long text repeated to trigger kvcache","another long text","long 3","long 4"],"client_batching":"explicit"}' | jq '.'
```

carol_customer: Ran it, got the same dim mix. Response snippet: `[{"id":"req_8a3f1c2b","embedding_len":512},{"id":"req_8a3f1c2c","embedding_len":768}, ...]`. Logged the exact curl output to our support ticket.

sara_ml: OK that matches the kernel fallback. Likely a quantized kernel selection bug when sequences cross a length threshold inside the same batch. Two action items: 1) collect debug bundle from the node that served the 512 outputs (gpu-12) 2) get minimal repro that toggles length to cross threshold so we can run locally in the CI harness.

alex_support: Jordan — can you grab a debug bundle (include /var/log/redwood/runtime.log, /proc/gpu_info, kernel selection trace) for node gpu-12 and upload to the support artifact store. Tag with the three req IDs.

jordan_infra: Bundle collected and uploaded: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/support/debug/1979991234/gpu-12-bundle.tar.gz. I also toggled runtime flag `force_kern=quant_safe` on a canary for 2m; early test batch from our internal repro returned all 768s.

carol_customer: I can test again if you want.

alex_support: Please do. Also, when you reproduce, include header `X-Debug-Request: true` so our traces link the request to the bundle.

carol_customer: Re-tested with flag — all embeddings now 768. Thanks. Leaving test logs in the ticket with header X-Debug-Request.

sara_ml: Great. We'll schedule a patch to the kernel selector to avoid fallback to incompatible quantized kernel when model variant expects 768. Next steps: PR with unit test + canary release.

alex_support: Summary for the ticket: root cause appears to be kernel fallback on mixed-length batches triggering a 512-dim quantized path. Mitigation: temporarily set `force_kern=quant_safe` for affected nodes + patch in next runtime release. I'll update the customer and close after the patch lands. :thumbsup:

debugbot: Incident note created — INC-2025-441: embedding-dim-fallback.linked_artifact: https://internal.artifacts/redwood/support/debug/1979991234/gpu-12-bundle.tar.gz
